objective: T-20260928-18: add the missing VIX and PUTW data so the two ETF rules blocked only by missing data in batch 2 (dir:spy_sso_tlt_vix_regime_rotation and dir:put_credit_spread_income) can actually be screened. Mid-task scope change (interactive session, 2026-09-28): the owner decided not to pursue cross-asset strategies (bonds/gold/commodities/dollar), which drops VIX_REGIME_SPY_SSO_TLT (its bear leg holds TLT). VIX (FRED VIXCLS) was still fetched into data/research/vix/ for later equity-only VIX-timing use. This dossier's remaining, sole objective is to check whether PUTW data can be added and, if so, preregister and screen PUTW_HOLD (buy-and-hold PUTW, monthly) as the honest proxy for dir:put_credit_spread_income's weekly SPY put-writing claim.
target_regime_and_horizon: Same frozen screen_lane windows as every other batch: select 2023-09-18..2025-12-31, anchor 2024-01-08..2026-09-17, holdout 2026-01-02..2026-09-17 (contaminated, reference only), stress 2016-05-02..2023-09-15. PUTW itself only exists since 2016-02-24 (see wisdomtree_putw_launch_2016), so the stress window would start at first_valid_signal_date, not at the stated window start -- same convention screen_lane already applies via window_actual_start for any candidate whose universe postdates a window.
existing_solution_comparison: `oc research directions check vix regime spy sso tlt putw put write income` (run before any new work) returned the exact two existing registry rows verbatim: dir:spy_sso_tlt_vix_regime_rotation (not_executable, VIX missing) and dir:put_credit_spread_income (not_executable, PUTW missing, with the exact same fetch_symbol_list.py/data/sip-delisted/daily blocker cited in reports/research/iterations/h20260928_05_registry_etf_batch2/data-feasibility.json). No third mechanism or new claim is introduced here; this round only tries to clear the data blocker batch 2 already diagnosed, and goes one step further by checking Alpaca itself (both the trading-asset list and the SIP market-data API) rather than only the local shard-layout question batch 2 stopped at.
remaining_evidence_gap: Batch 2 established that fetch_symbol_list.py (the repo's existing arbitrary-symbol ingestion path) writes to a separate tree (data/sip-delisted/daily/) that the screen_lane/screen_batch harness does not read, and that editing screen_lane.py/screen_batch.py to read a second tree is out of scope. What batch 2 did not check is whether Alpaca -- our only market-data and paper-broker vendor -- carries PUTW at all, independent of the local shard question. That is the decisive test this round runs.
negative_experiments_checked: reports/research/iterations/h20260928_05_registry_etf_batch2/data-feasibility.json's data_gaps_noted_not_fetched.PUTW entry (2026-09-28): PUTW absent from data/sip/daily, not fetched because of the shard-layout/loader-tree mismatch. This round does not repeat that check; it extends it with a direct Alpaca API probe (see cheapest_decisive_test) that was not run in batch 2.
cost_and_execution_assumptions: Unchanged from every prior screen_lane round: signal at bar close, fill at next bar open, 10bp primary / 20bp stress per side, remainder of any weight vector to SHY. PUTW_HOLD would be declared freq M (matching the fund's own monthly option-roll cadence per wisdomtree_putw_launch_2016/cboe_put_index_factsheet_2026), weight 1.0 PUTW, evaluated against the owner's 2026-09-28 relaxed K1 (median-offset Sharpe >=80% of S3's anchor and stress, positive 20bp CAGR) / K2 (S3+candidate inverse-vol blend beats vol-matched control by >=0.05 Sharpe) rule -- contingent on the data blocker below being resolved, which it was not.
stop_condition: Decisive test result (see cheapest_decisive_test): Alpaca's trading API returns 'asset not found for PUTW' (TradingClient.get_asset, paper account, 2026-09-28) and Alpaca's SIP market-data API returns 0 rows for PUTW over the most recent 10 trading days (StockHistoricalDataClient.get_stock_bars, feed=sip, 2026-09-28), confirmed against XYLD/QYLD/JEPI/JEPQ/DIVO all resolving correctly with the identical call as a methodology sanity check. PUTW is not merely missing from our local archive (the batch-2 finding) -- it is not served by Alpaca at all, for either trading or market data. No existing or newly-written ingestion script can fetch what the vendor does not have. This is a harder, vendor-level blocker than the shard-layout question in the brief's 'if impossible without restructuring shards, stop and report' clause: no amount of local data engineering (shard-safe or otherwise) fixes it. PUTW_HOLD is preregistered below for the record and marked not_executable; no scripts/screen_batch.py run occurs in this iteration because there is no runnable candidate (VIX_REGIME_SPY_SSO_TLT dropped by owner scope decision, PUTW_HOLD blocked at the vendor level).

sources.claim: WisdomTree launched the CBOE S&P 500 PutWrite Strategy Fund (PUTW) on NYSE Arca on 2016-02-24, tracking the Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT) before fees; the fund sells at-the-money, European-style, one-month S&P 500 Index puts against a fully collateralized T-bill account and rebalances (rolls the options) monthly.
sources.market_and_period: US, WisdomTree CBOE S&P 500 PutWrite Strategy Fund (PUTW), NYSE Arca, launch press release.
sources.applicability: Grounds PUTW_HOLD's proxy inception date (2016-02-24) and monthly-rebalance mechanism in candidate-manifest.json.
sources.limitations: Marketing press release, not the fund's prospectus or NAV history.
sources.independent_replication: Cross-checked against the CBOE PUT index's own official fact sheet (cboe_put_index_factsheet_2026).

sources.claim: Cboe's own official strategy-index fact sheet (data as of 2026-08-31) states the Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT) has an index launch date of 2007-06-20 (first value date 2007-01-03) and reports, from 2007-01-03 through the fact-sheet date, an annualized return of 7.1%, annualized volatility 10.7%, maximum drawdown -32.7%, beta 0.6, Sharpe ratio 0.52 and Sortino ratio 0.69 (vs. 11.0%/15.4%/-50.9%/1.0/0.61/0.92 for the S&P 500 Total Return Index over the same window); SPX puts are struck at-the-money and sold monthly, usually on the 3rd Friday.
sources.market_and_period: Cboe S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT), 2007-01-03 through 2026-08-31, monthly SPX at-the-money put writing vs. T-bill collateral.
sources.applicability: Independent, official-exchange confirmation of the PUT index mechanism PUTW tracks; long-run index Sharpe used as context only.
sources.limitations: Index-level statistics, not net of PUTW's own 0.38% expense ratio or tracking error.
sources.independent_replication: Matches the WisdomTree launch press release's own citation of the same mechanism.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: Before writing any batch module, probe Alpaca directly for PUTW: (1) TradingClient(paper=True).get_asset('PUTW') to check it exists in Alpaca's tradable US-equity asset list (the same list scripts/fetch_sip_universe.py's load_universe() and scripts/update_sip_archive.py's append_new_symbols() both depend on); (2) StockHistoricalDataClient.get_stock_bars(symbol='PUTW', feed='sip') for the most recent 10 trading days, to check whether Alpaca's market-data side serves it even if the trading side does not. Sanity-checked the exact same two calls against XYLD/QYLD/JEPI/JEPQ/DIVO, all already known-tradable ETFs.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: get_asset('PUTW') returns a tradable asset, or get_stock_bars returns >=1 row -- either would mean PUTW is fetchable through an existing Alpaca-backed ingestion path (fetch_symbol_list.py at minimum), and the remaining question becomes the batch-2 shard-layout/loader-tree question, not vendor availability.
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: Both calls return nothing for PUTW while the five known-tradable control ETFs all resolve correctly -- confirms Alpaca (our only data/broker vendor) does not carry PUTW at all, a vendor-level blocker no local script can work around.
